items.stem: You must place a line endpoint exactly on an existing circle's centre. Which feature ensures precision?

options.rationale: Correct: object snaps lock onto exact geometric points such as a circle centre.

options.text: Zooming in and clicking by eye
options.rationale: Clicking by eye is imprecise even when zoomed.
Layers organise objects; they do not snap geometry.
Units do not place points precisely on existing geometry.

items.stem: In which space do you typically set a plot scale and place a titleblock for printing?

options.rationale: Correct: layouts/paper space hold titleblocks and set plot scale via viewports.
Model space holds the real-scale geometry; plotting setup lives in layouts.
The command line issues commands; it is not a drawing space.
Properties edits object attributes, not plot layout.

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to use layers in a drawing?

options.text: Control visibility and plotting of groups of objects
options.rationale: Correct: layers let you show/hide and control plotting by group.

options.text: Assign consistent colour, linetype and lineweight by discipline
options.rationale: Correct: layer properties standardise appearance by category.
Layers organise objects; they do not add geometric precision.

options.text: Replace the need for object snaps
options.rationale: Layers and object snaps serve different purposes.

items.explanation: Correct: layers let you show/hide and control plotting by group.
